contexts.statement: Review the mathematical assertions of the 29 inventoried old artifacts and the staged manuscript reference entry; no inherited error-search objective, whole-paper certification, novelty assertion, or acceptance. Geometry is reviewed under the exact fixed-resolution terminal-fourfold hypotheses.

definitions.a: ordinary LOG discrepancy; relative canonical coefficient a-1
definitions.g: specified globally projective resolution, smooth source, isomorphism over Yreg, SNC exceptional divisor, principalized singular ideal with full inverse-image support
definitions.global_place: prime on a proper bimeromorphic model of the whole compact Y, modulo common-model strict transform; not a local branch
definitions.T0: connected smooth finite-punctured part of irreducible singular curve T, with W and V local systems
definitions.N_T: distinct exceptional primes E on g with g(E)=T and a(E;Y,0)=2

claims.natural_statement: Every one of the 29 inventoried artifacts and the reference-input/tooling entry has an explicit disposition; all eight CP claims and all versions, Section 5, Appendix A, both retired shortcuts, finite checking and attribution are substantively assessed in the 14 indexed units. This is a review-coverage assertion, not a statement that all old theorems are true.
The canonical restriction W->V is a surjection of local systems and has the asserted stalkwise interpretation.

The entire projective analytic scheme family over T algebraizes via an explicit proper ambient embedding. Fiber line bundles span W rationally, including nonreduced scheme fibers. Countably many finite-type parameter spaces and finite multisections imply finite monodromy. Poincare duality and finite-group averaging give b independent invariant lifts through W->V.

Invariant fiber classes lift integrally near a full loop-preserving Runge compact. The lifts have actual Cartier divisor representatives on g inverse of a Stein neighborhood. Fujino's theorem gives a small projective crepant terminal model over the full compact Kprime. The finite prescribed Weil divisors have one common Cartier multiple before restriction to a smaller core.
The degree map Q^b->Q^s is injective, accounting for every fiber curve, normalization-cover sheet, and nilpotent thickening.

Every log-discrepancy-two place centered on the singular curve is already on the specified principalizing resolution. Restriction to a pi1-surjective curve core is a bijection of all local and global discrepancy-two places. Distinct surface centers on the small model give distinct global primes.
For Y compact Kahler under the exact fixed-resolution hypotheses, b<=N_T for distinct global primes, by b<=s<=N_T.
The curve bound and globalization bijection hold for compact complex Y without Kahlerness, retaining global projectivity of the specified resolution and every other hypothesis.

Summing the curve bounds over distinct centers gives sum b_T<=tau_Y(Q). With the separate Section 05 topological inequality one obtains the branch inequality. The junction and termination consequences additionally require separate Section 07 weights and other programs.

The projective quadric cone times P1 is a terminal fourfold with the specified principalizing resolution. Its unique global exceptional prime has relative canonical coefficient 1 and log discrepancy 2. The O(-1,-1) circle-bundle link gives constant V of rank 1 and hence b=N_T=1. The small-resolution degree matrix is [1].

The transverse-surface argument in Appendix A supplies terminal-fourfold smoothness in codimension two. A terminal normal surface has no exceptional curves on its minimal resolution. A smooth codimension-c blowup has log discrepancy c. Composition adds positive relative canonical coefficients, not their negatives and not the log discrepancies themselves.
One cannot infer a count of distinct global primes by counting branches after dropping the curve loops: a transitive two-sheet cover can split.
A surjective equivariant quotient need not surject on invariant sections for infinite monodromy; the displayed unipotent quotient is a counterexample to that linear-algebra shortcut.

The unchanged standard-library verifier recomputes the supplied exact certificate with active assertions. It checks 617 ordered permutation-generator pairs on 1-4 sheets, one S3 invariant-lift example, and 624 bounded rational sign cases. It checks four sharpness blowup charts and independently replays the saved Jacobian Gysin rank. No Lean source or compiler evidence is supplied; geometry is not mechanically certified.

The eight CP assertions form one shared geometric argument, not eight independently proved new theorems. The ledger contains 17 claim records, including assumption-enrichment versions and one historical campaign objective. The two live old routes share obligations; the two retired routes are separately assessed. Five staged manuscript directories are reference inputs, not five additional Argus draft results.

routes.retired_because: A simply connected disc can split a transitive two-sheet cover into two branches, so its local surface count does not bound distinct global primes. This is a failed counting inference, not a fourfold counterexample; retain a pi1-surjective core.

For the infinite unipotent action [[1,1],[0,1]] with quotient (x,y)->y, the quotient is surjective and equivariant but invariant vectors map to zero. A quotient alone cannot justify invariant lifts; geometric finite monodromy must first be proved.
